title: The Day of the Science Fair
subject: Code
description: Judging is in forty-eight minutes and the prototype just died. Every choice you make changes how this ends.

examples.prompt: A sensor reads 0, then 138, then 0, then 0, then 141. What does that pattern suggest?
choices: The sensor is dead and needs replacing
A connection is making contact only some of the time
The batteries are flat
examples.explain: A dead sensor reads 0 every single time. Readings that come back are a sensor that works — so the fault is between the sensor and the board.

examples.prompt: Your robot drives perfectly straight on the classroom carpet. Should you expect the same on the polished gym floor?
choices: Yes — straight is straight
No — the wheels grip differently, so it may drift
examples.explain: Different surfaces mean different grip. A calibration tuned on carpet is a calibration for carpet. Test where it will actually run.

examples.prompt: Your board resets whenever the motors strain against something. What kind of problem is that usually?
choices: A bug in the code
A power problem — the voltage dips below what the board needs
A broken motor
examples.explain: Straining motors pull extra current. If the supply can't deliver it, voltage sags and the board reboots. Nothing is wrong with the code at all.

quiz.prompt: Before changing anything, what should an engineer do first?
choices: Replace the part that seems most likely to be broken
Find out what is actually happening, using real data
Reflash the code to start from a clean slate
quiz.explain: Changing things before you understand the problem is guessing. The Serial Monitor shows you what is really going on — look before you touch.

quiz.prompt: A connection works when you test it on the bench but fails once the robot is driving. Why?
choices: Driving uses different code
Vibration works friction-held connections loose
The sensor gets tired
quiz.explain: Breadboard connections are held by friction alone. A robot rolling across a floor shakes constantly, and that shaking is exactly what a friction fit cannot survive.

quiz.prompt: Why does testing on the surface you'll actually demo on matter?
choices: It doesn't — a robot drives the same everywhere
Different surfaces grip differently, so the robot moves differently
The judges expect to see you practise
quiz.explain: "Works in the lab" and "works in the field" are two different claims. Only one of them is the one being judged.

quiz.prompt: Your board resets every time the motors work hard. What is the real cause?
choices: The motors are drawing more current than the supply can give
There is an infinite loop in the code
The LCD is using too much memory
quiz.explain: This is a power budget problem, not a code problem. Add up what every part needs, then check your supply can actually deliver it.

quiz.prompt: You are out of time and something still isn't fixed. What is the honest thing to do?
choices: Say nothing and hope the judges don't notice
Know what the limitation is, and be able to explain it
Make a fast change you have not tested
quiz.explain: Judges have seen plenty of things break. An engineer who knows exactly why theirs broke is showing the most valuable skill there is.
